Author: Deepak Roshan
Bench: Deepak Roshan
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi

 Chhuttu Manjhi @ Santosh Murmu ..... Petit
 Versus
 The State of Jharkhand ..... Opposit

entities.text: High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Deepak Roshan

For the Petitioner : Mr. Randhir Kumar, Advocate  For the State : Mr. Azeemuddin, APP  ---------
 06/ 10.11.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The instant application has been preferred by the petitioner for grant of regular bail for the offence registered under Sections 452, 354, 354(B), 323, 379, 506/34 of the Indian Penal Code and later on Section 376 of the IPC has been added.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner has falsely been implicated in this case for the reason that he is also in the same business of selling local liquor as that of informant and it is basically business rivalry between the informant and this petitioner and due to that there was also a fight prior to this incident.

He further submits that though there is allegation of recording the incidence but neither mobile phone has been seized by the Investigating Officer nor the torn clothes were sent for expert opinion; this itself shows that the entire allegation is false and the victim is none trustworthy.
Learned APP for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submits that the charge has already been framed in this case.
However, he could not point out as to whether the torn clothes have been sent for expert opinion and/or the mobile has been seized by the police and sent for having report.
5. Having regard to the facts of the case and manner of occurrence as alleged coupled with the fact that charge has been framed in this case, I am inclined to enlarge this petitioner on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail.

The petitioner shall furnish bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (Ten thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II, FTC, Bermo at Tenughat, in connection with S.T. Case No. 58 of 2023, arising out of Jaridih P.S. Case No. 229 of 2022, corresponding to G.R. No. 1389 of 2022.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-II, FTC, Bermo at Tenughat
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
6. It is made clear that the bail is granted to the petitioner subject to following conditions:
i) The petitioner shall not do any act to threaten the witnesses.
ii) He shall appear on each and every date before the learned trial court.
If any of the condition is not complied, learned trial court would be at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner.

7. It goes without saying that since the charge has already been framed in this case the learned trial court shall conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible, preferabaly within the period of six months from the date of this order.
(Deepak Roshan, J.) Pramanik/
